decisions.summary: _trim_to_service loses its two vertex-popping loops; the existing two-pass 4 ft walk is the one pull-back for every end, popping a vertex only once the end is within 4 ft of it; the comment above the walk is rewritten to say so; the claim line stands unchanged.
decisions.why: This is 385 T126, an open non-process task moved into 405 by the GM's routing ('everything else moves into a new feature') and worked as 385 worked its tasks (FR-001). It brings the code into line with its own unchanged claim and the 0246 research ('pulled back to the last house it serves'), which the impl-drift round recorded DRIFTED. Nothing the request or the spec asks for is narrowed: no end, lane or case is excluded, and the claim is not weakened.

decisions.summary: Exit (e) conform the code to the claim rather than amend the claim; a coarser walk step was weighed and refused, keeping the existing 4 ft grain.
decisions.why: Conforming to the stated claim and research keeps existing documented behavior the request does not touch; refusing a coarser step changes nothing and carves out no case.

decisions.summary: A unit test red at HEAD on a run whose long last segment passes a house within 60 ft partway; claims round on the changed unit; gate and landing cohort.
decisions.why: Verification that only fails when the fixed behavior is absent - enforcement of the task, plus the standing 385 per-task checks FR-001 carries; no new behavior, map or tier is added.

decisions.summary: _sweep_dangling_ends loses its two vertex-popping loops; each end walks in along its last segment 4 ft at a time, dropping a vertex only once within 4 ft of it, with the 269 E4 hold asked before each step; docstring and claim updated to name the walk and its grain.
decisions.why: This is the moved 385 task T128 itself (worked per FR-001 under the GM's 2026-10-19 routing of everything not process into 405). The walk is the mechanism the task names: it brings the code into line with the 0246 rule (pull back to the last house served) and covers every end. Keeping the existing E4 hold carves no case out of the task's goal. The 4 ft grain matches the existing _trim_to_service step, and D8 removes nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: An end's reach is asked of the other lanes' segments minus those within _TOUCH_GAP of the lane's OTHER end (as _trim_to_service's serves does, feature 261), so a link off a way with nothing at its far end walks back to nothing and is emptied, as the pop did; claimed as GUESS on 0246.
decisions.why: This defines what serves an end. It is not an exception to the task. Every end is still walked in, and nothing is popped. Reaching only the way the lane springs from serves nothing, so the 0246 rule that an end reaching nothing is pulled back covers this case. D9 keeps the current outcome for a stub (emptied) and stops the new walk from leaving tails the pop never left, so it carries out the task's goal rather than narrowing it. The research page is silent on this point, and the plan says so openly: it labels D9 O (feature 261) and claims it as GUESS on 0246. Neither the GM's request nor the spec index says anything that D9 departs from.

decisions.summary: _web_cut_lines._extent reads only the houses within WEB_REACH_FT of the cut; the 'or along' whole-cluster fallback is removed and the invariant (web_cuts places every cut within reach of the house that called for it) is stated in a comment; no map changes because the fallback never ran.
decisions.why: The task moved here under the GM's 2026-10-19 routing (everything not a process task moves into 405) and is worked per FR-001; its own title is 'a web lane's span has no whole-cluster fallback'. Removing the fallback is that task, conforming the code to 0246's rule that a lane runs along the houses it serves. Nothing the request or the moved task asks for is narrowed; the 'no map changes' premise is stated as measured (a read of the code on 2026-10-21), not assumed.

decisions.summary: A unit test over many coordinate sets that every cut web_cuts makes has a house within its reach and every cut line spans only those houses plus the 30 ft pad.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the task's own rule (no lane laid along houses it does not serve); delete the requested behavior and the test has nothing left to check. Verification, not new behavior.

decisions.summary: The DRIFTED claim is settled by making the code conform to the research rather than amending the claim.
decisions.why: The task title asks for the code to hold no whole-cluster fallback; conforming the code is the reading the task names, and no part of the request is excepted.

decisions.summary: The plan is written one section per task, each at that task's start, against docs/approach-checklist.md.
decisions.why: A drafting convention for the plan document; it narrows nothing the request or FR-001 (each task worked as 385 worked its tasks, checklist part A answered) asks for.

decisions.summary: Lands open: T01-T31 - the feature may reach main with any of its 31 tasks still open.
decisions.why: The GM's 2026-10-20 start asks for one claim fixed and then the numbers reviewed before deciding what next (FR-004, SC-002: a report before a second task), so landing with the remaining tasks open is what was asked. Declaring a task may land open does not drop it: SC-001 still requires every task ticked, and no task is removed or exempted from FR-001/FR-002.

decisions.why: A finding on code T12 did not change, filed as a task of this feature as FR-002 and the GM's 2026-10-19 words ('keep findings on code a task didn't change as new tasks') require; it makes a plan review read the GM's words verbatim, which is the review's own contract.

decisions.why: Keeps the review on the GM's verbatim words rather than a possibly trimmed quote; narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: task-add next_id takes the largest id of tasks.md boxes and plan.md/plan-done.md '## T<n>' headings, plus one, ignoring ids quoted in titles
decisions.why: FR-002 found work; conforms task-add to 385 T64 D83's 'next free id' instead of reading quoted ids such as '(385 T147)'.

decisions.summary: only the clone's active task (plan_gate.active_task) of this feature, open and not in L7R_LAND_TICKS, holds a push; GM-review box, carried and unstarted tasks never hold; the push's refusal names the active task and 'make land F= T='
decisions.why: Directly answers the GM's 2026-10-20 'I do not want each landing to owe a lands open line ... that's going to slow things down', while keeping 330's protection of mid-task work. 375 D12's effect (the GM-review box does not hold a landing) is preserved. Residual, not a ruling: the hold reaches mid-task work only when 'make task-start' was run in the clone, so the mechanism's reach depends on task-start being required before work.

decisions.summary: the **Lands open**: line is no longer read; task-add stops writing it and the [lands-open] mark; the tick's 'mark the tooling did not put here' refusal is removed and any mark is inert text
decisions.why: The consequence of the GM's 'no lands open line': with only the active task holding, the line, the mark and the refusal that policed the mark have nothing left to do. The tick's refusal guarded self-exemption through a mark that no longer exempts anything.

decisions.summary: keeping the line without its review was weighed and refused
decisions.why: The GM asked for no line at all; keeping it would be the thing he declined.

decisions.summary: scripts/land.py / make land: pass 1 prints every cheap refusal (tick refusals but the landed one, uncommitted work, owed ledger rows, claims gate, review gate, holding rule) together and exits 2; pass 2 runs gate-stamp check, 'make done' when the stamp does not cover the content, 'make cohort-landing' when the cohort gate refuses, commits gate regenerations under pool/, pushes with L7R_LAND_TICKS, ticks each task; land-batch.py a shim
decisions.why: Answers the GM's 'the landing being the biggest cost is something that we need to do something about' and his ask to make and work the tooling changes. Every gate still runs and still refuses; only the order and the hand steps between them change. Auto-running make done / cohort-landing and committing their pool/ output does what the session did by hand after each refusal; no gate is skipped.

decisions.summary: running the gate and the cohort in parallel deferred to a measurement of its own (memory cap, feature 315)
decisions.why: A deferral of one option, not a narrowing of anything the GM asked; nothing requested is removed.

decisions.summary: in push_cmd the fetch, the delta, the holding rule and review-gate.sh run before push_checks.py and claims-gate.sh; checks and messages otherwise unchanged
decisions.why: Reorder only, serving the GM's landing-cost ask; the holding rule is still judged against the fetched main. D6 moves claims-gate.sh behind as well, which approach item 5 does not name but item 4's current-order note implies; no check is dropped.

decisions.summary: sync-with-main.sh done runs push_cmd then render_sync_background (lock and log as the prompt hook's), printing where the log is; render-sync stays foreground for a hand run
decisions.why: Render-sync still runs after every landing, so the GM's 2026-08-12 reason (renders in main kept fresh) is kept; only the landing stops waiting on it, which is the GM's 2026-10-20 landing-cost ask. Residual: a session must not tell the GM to look at a render until the background log shows it finished, or the 2026-08-12 round trip recurs.

decisions.summary: T36: the bundle marks changed lines; the agent tags a finding resting on no changed line and no added/reworded claim '[outside the change]'; classify carries it when UNCLAIMED or its claim matches the base; make land runs the carry first.
decisions.why: Proposal A, approved by the GM 2026-10-21, and the plainer reading of the GM's 2026-10-19 rule ('findings on code a task didn't change as new tasks'): the finding is filed as a task instead of refusing. It changes the operative sentence of 385 FR-013 ('a finding on changed code ... still introduced') at line rather than unit granularity; that is what A asks, not a carve-out from it.

decisions.why: Proposal B ('named first'); naming is what the title promises and nothing in the request or spec asks for a refusal.

decisions.why: Proposal C; it conforms the clock to the existing rule (385) that a wait on the GM is not the session's time.

decisions.why: Proposal D; it makes 371/395's existing tracing reach the claims bundles and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: T40: changed_lines widened to every line of each enclosing function; an on-path gap mapped to a baseline line reached only by quick-tier tests (or none) is refused.
decisions.why: Proposal F's own subject ('judges a changed function's every line'); it widens what the preflight checks.

decisions.summary: T40: with no baseline, today's rule (on-path gaps deferred to the gate).
decisions.why: Physically impossible otherwise: without a baseline coverage.db there is no evidence of what the rolls reach, and the only alternative, running the rolls, breaks FR-004's 'takes seconds'. The gate's 100% floor still judges the line, so nothing escapes; T14's case (an unchanged line in a changed function with a baseline) is fully caught.

decisions.summary: T40: a line the delta changed has no baseline line and keeps today's rule (the gate judges it on the hamlet path).
decisions.why: Same ground: a changed line has no baseline counterpart, so no evidence exists for the preflight to read in seconds; the gate still judges it. The purpose (catch the T14 class, an unchanged line in a changed function) is untouched.

decisions.summary: T41: a .py change outside page/browser whose gate-stamp semantic_bytes are equal is a move the gate does not see; it passes the guard and the tree check.
decisions.why: Proposal E, and it reuses the stamp's own accepted ruling (385 T57) that a docstring/comment edit is not a change the gate exercised, so tree check and stamp cannot disagree. Not a new exception.

decisions.summary: T41: the claims round's records (dev/claims-index.json, dev/claims-pages.json, dev/review-ledger.md, specs/*/ found.jsonl, arbiter.jsonl, claims-carried.jsonl) and make claims-checked / claims-triaged / append pass the gate-write guard (385 FR-010) and the tree check.
decisions.why: Implied by the GM's own words: E is 'the gate runs beside the claims round', which cannot happen while FR-010 refuses the claims round's own writes. Each path is a claims-round record the gate does not exercise.

decisions.summary: T41: specs/*/plan.md and specs/*/tasks.md of ANY feature are also 'unseen', so any git add/commit, Edit or Write of them passes the gate-write guard and leaves the running gate's tree check unmoved.
decisions.why: A separate case bundled under the claims-round argument. The claims round's only named writer of these is the carry (385 FR-013: claims-carry 'writes the task box'), which touches the landing feature's tasks.md (and plan.md only if the carry writes a block - D15 does not say). As written the slice lets a hand Edit of any feature's plan or tasks through the FR-010 guard mid-gate, which is not the claims round and is not what E asked. It also fails D15's own definition 'a move the gate does not see': 375 FR-004 runs spec-lint inside the gate, and plan.md is what the plan-stage gate digests. Fix: scope it to the writes the carry makes (the active feature's tasks.md, plus its plan.md if and only if the carry writes a block there, said in D15), not every writer on every spec.

The predicate is path-level, so a hand Edit of that one tasks.md also passes mid-gate; that is the scope round 1 prescribed (one file of the feature being landed, not every spec). Whether spec-lint reads tasks.md was not verifiable from the bundle and is not asserted here.
